body.justification: The full-data interval has exact finite-sample conditional coverage and the sharp four-channel expected-length rate under fixed strict donor-envelope slack.
body.gap: Coverage and the upper length bound remain valid at equality, where only the treated, smoothing, and spacing lower rate is asserted.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain finite-sample conditionally honest inference throughout the compatible class and an explicit disclosure of when donor-optimal expected length is proved.
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\},
\]
and first condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N)\).  On each successful fit, the definition of \(a_{sti}\) gives polynomial reproduction:
\[
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
a_{sti}b_r(u_{st})^\top
=e_0^\top G_s^{-1}
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{st}b_r(u_{st})b_r(u_{st})^\top
=e_0^\top.
\tag{23}
\]
Apply (23) to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\).  The Holder remainder from \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness} then gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{24}
\]
After multiplying by \(\pi_s\) and summing over cohorts, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define the unit-cluster historical fluctuations
\[
U_{si}=\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^Ta_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}, followed by \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{si}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N]=0.
\tag{25}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes these variables conditionally independent over \((s,i)\).  Because \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(U_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^T|a_{sti}|.
\tag{26}
\]
For a conditionally centered random variable in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of the exponential bounds its moment generating function by the endpoint mixture having the same mean; differentiating the logarithm of that mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\tag{27}
\]
Multiplication of (27) over the independent unit clusters, exponential Markov inequality, and optimization over \(v>0\), repeated for \(-U\), yield
\[
P_P\!\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^S\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{28}
\]
The entire calendar history of one unit is one cluster in (28); no temporal outcome independence or mixing is used.

Similarly, define
\[
V_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers \(V_{si}\) given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\); donor independence permits adjoining the donors, and cross-unit independence gives conditional independence.  By consistency and \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}, its conditional range length is at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  Applying (27) gives
\[
P_P\!\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^S\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}V_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{29}
\]
A union bound combines (28)--(29), so dependence between a unit's historical path and event outcome is allowed.

For donor calibration, define only in this proof
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^NY_j,
\qquad D=Sd.
\]
Conditional donor replication gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y_j\mid E_0]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\tag{30}
\]
In the expansion of \(\|W_N\|_2^4\), every term containing a singleton sample index has conditional expectation zero.  The all-equal terms and the three pairings, together with \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}, give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{31}
\]
For the proof event \(\mathcal D_N=\{\|W_N\|_2\le q_N\}\), Markov's inequality and the definition of \(q_N\) imply
\[
P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)
\le\frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}
=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{32}
\]
Projection onto the cube cannot increase Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), because \(z_0\) lies in that cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds therefore give, on \(\mathcal D_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\widetilde z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\bar Z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\frac{q_N}{\sqrt N}
=\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{33}
\]
On the good sample, \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\).  The upper inequality in \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (33) then show
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa
=A_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{34}
\]

Let \(\mathcal G\) be the selector-and-radius good event in \texttt{def:honest-interval}; it is measurable with respect to \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N)\).  On \(\mathcal G^c\), the interval is \([-B,B]\).  By \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}, each conditional mean contrast in \texttt{def:target} lies in \([-B,B]\), and the positive cohort weights sum to one; hence \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\).  On \(\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N\), \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, (24), and (34) decompose the estimation error into the event and historical fluctuations plus two terms bounded by \(A_L\) and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Therefore noncoverage implies failure of (28) or (29).  Iterated conditioning and (32) yield, for all positive sample sizes,
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)\\
&\quad+\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf1_{\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N}
P_P\{\text{historical failure or event failure}
\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N\}
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]\\
&\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}
+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{35}
\]
No selector-tail probability enters (35), which proves exact finite-sample conditional coverage.

We next bound expected length.  On successful fits, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})
c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{36}
\]
The support of \(K\) and the same deterministic absolute-weight bound imply
\[
A_L\le C\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\tag{37}
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(\lambda\), conditionally on \(E_0\) and \(\widetilde z_s\), and then integrate over the donor sample.  Cauchy--Schwarz over the fixed cohorts gives
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathcal G}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2},
\tag{38}
\]
where \(N^{-\lambda/2}\le N^{-\kappa/2}\) follows from \(N\ge1\) and \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  Since \(D\), \(B\), and \(\alpha\) are fixed, (31) gives \(q_N\le C\), and therefore
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}
\le CN^{-\kappa/2}
=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{39}
\]
The selector lemma gives
\[
\sup_P P_P(\mathcal G^c\mid E_0)
\le CR_{\star,\beta}
\tag{40}
\]
along the stated arrays; the deterministic condition \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\) holds eventually.  The fallback length is at most \(2B\), the nonfallback length is at most \(2H_\alpha\), and eventually \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Combining (36)--(40) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{41}
\]
This argument uses only the upper fourth-moment envelope, so it is valid both for \(B>D^2\) and for \(B=D^2\).

It remains to prove the appropriate lower bounds.  Let
\[
\mathcal Q_B=
\begin{cases}
\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\},&B>D^2,\\
\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp}\},&B=D^2.
\end{cases}
\tag{42}
\]
For every \(q\in\mathcal Q_B\), use the pair from \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}.  The perturbation constants in the treated, smoothing, and donor constructions can be multiplied by a sufficiently small fixed factor: equations (7), (10), and (18) in that lemma's proof then make their affinities arbitrarily close to one by (22), while their target separations retain the same rate with a smaller positive constant.  In the spacing construction, reducing the fixed rare-block activation constant makes the no-active-block probability, and hence affinity, arbitrarily close to one, while multiplying separation only by a fixed positive power of that constant.  Thus, for the fixed \(\alpha<1/2\), all applicable pairs may be chosen with
\[
A_q:=\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}
\ge2\alpha+a_0
\tag{43}
\]
for a fixed \(a_0>0\), and with target values \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) satisfying
\[
|\theta_1-\theta_0|\ge cR_q^{1/2}.
\tag{44}
\]

Let \(I\) be finite-sample conditionally honest and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\) be the conditional overlap measure.  Uniform honesty and domination of \(\mu_q\) by both laws imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge\mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\mid E_0\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\mid E_0\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha
\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{45}
\]
On this event \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Hence (44)--(45) give
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{46}
\]
When \(B>D^2\), maximizing (46) over all four channels yields
\[
c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{47}
\]
When \(B=D^2\), maximizing over the three asserted channels yields only
\[
c_\alpha
\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}^{1/2},
\tag{48}
\]
and no universal donor lower bound is used or claimed.  If intervals are merely uniformly asymptotically conditionally honest, then for every \(\epsilon>0\) their two noncoverage probabilities are eventually at most \(\alpha+\epsilon\).  Taking \(\epsilon<a_0/4\) replaces the last bound in (45) by \(a_0-2\epsilon\ge a_0/2\), preserving (47) or (48).  Equations (35), (41), and (47)--(48) prove every asserted coverage and expected-length conclusion.  Finally, equation (1) in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} shows that \(B<D^2\) is an empty configuration, so no substantive minimax assertion is assigned to it.
